1	# Leads
2	
3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine sends a daily (and monthly) gas nomination as a Word attachment to the HPL scheduler. Several Enron staff are copied, and someone has to re-key the volumes and confirm them back.: The same 'Calpine Daily Gas Nomination' email with 'CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc' arrives near-daily from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001. The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace Calpine's emailed daily Word-document gas nomination (plus duplicate phone call and confirmation email) with a structured feed/portal entry and exception-only confirmation.

TODAY: Every gas day Calpine Fuel Supply (Ricky Archer) emails a Word attachment "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc" to the HPL scheduler, copying 2-3 more Enron staff, often after already phoning it in. The scheduler opens the .doc, re-keys volumes into scheduling, and confirms back by email even when nothing changed.
Evidence:
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/579.eml (14 Dec 1999), Subject "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination", attachment " - CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc", to robert.lloyd, cc daren.farmer.
- corpus/williams-w3/inbox/143.eml (6 Mar 2000): "As we spoke of this morning." with "<<CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc>>" — the phone call and email duplicate each other.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/773.eml (8 Feb 2000): "FW: Calpine Daily Gas Nomination (REVISED)" — revisions resent as whole documents.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1245.eml (27 Jun 2000): "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination and Monthly (JULY) Nomination" with "CALPINE MONTHLY GAS NOMINATION___.doc" — a monthly nom too.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1310.eml (27 Jul 2000) cc "dfarmer@enron.com, mmccoy@enron.com, rcotten@enron.com"; corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1537.eml (21 Nov 2000) to aimee.lannou, same three cc's — same process ran for a year, recipient changes as staff rotate.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/795.eml: Darron Giron replies "Confirmed on my end. Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path." — confirmation emails are sent even when nothing changed.
- 22 files across the archive carry this subject, from Dec 1999 to 2001; the subject itself names it "Daily".

CHANGE: Calpine enters its nomination into a shared structured template (spreadsheet/CSV posted to a fixed location or an EDI/web nomination form) that loads into the scheduling system; standing nominations roll forward automatically and only changes generate a notice. The phone call and "no change" confirmation email are dropped; confirmation is automatic. The cc list gets nothing unless volumes change.

AFTER: Scheduler reviews an exception notice only on days with changes (verify and approve, ~2 min).

SAVINGS per gas day (all Enron people): scheduler open .doc + re-key + confirm reply ~6 min → ~1 min average (exceptions only) = 5 min; 3 cc'd staff opening/reading ~1 min each = 3 min; phone call duplicate on the Enron side ~2 min. Total ~10 min/day. Calpine's own time not counted. Frequency: daily per the subject "Daily Gas Nomination"; conservatively 21 business days/month (nominations are made business days, weekend noms often bundled). 10 × 21 = 210 min = 3.5 h/month × $85 = ~$298/month. Plus monthly nom (small, not counted).

No prompt-injection text was found in these messages.

Attached please find the Activity Survey for the month of May, 2000.

I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with 
this months data collection efforts.  Please pay particular attention this 
month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for 
data quality and timeliness.

The attached survey drives your costs from your activities to the commercial 
teams.  Please select your RCs, and fill in the driver quantity for the 
requested driver for the month of May. Please fill out the attached activity 
driver survey with May numbers for your RC and return to Shari Mao by end of 
day Friday, June 2.

Please note the following updates:
For Nat Gas, Sally Beck is interested in physical (as denoted as PH in the 
survey) vs. financial (as denoted as FI in the survey) numbers, please 
provide statistics accordingly
If a driver has not been updated per your request, please call or email 
Jennifer Reside
If you have additional updates / suggestions or items that need correction, 
please call or email Jennifer Reside

If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the 
surveyed data, please send the report to Jennifer Reside.  This will 
eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month.  If you would like 
us to collect this information from someone within your team beginning next 
month, please let Jennifer know.

Please contact Jennifer Reside x3-5971 with questions (Shari is on vacation 
this week), or if you are unable to complete the survey within the allotted 
time.

Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of May, 
2000.

I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with 
this months data collection efforts.  Please pay particular attention this 
month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for 
data quality and timeliness.

While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers. 
Please return these surveys to Shari Mao by end of day Friday, June 2.

The Nat Gas RC's will now see deal validation and transportation rate 
activities therefore, these surveys will be notably longer but will not 
necessarily take more time

PLEASE DO NOT TYPE ANY ACTIVITIES IN THE SURVEY.  Contact Jennifer Reside at 
#35971 to discuss how to proceed.

If you have any questions relating to the model or this survey, or are unable 
to meet the survey due date, please call Jennifer Reside at #35971 (Shari is 
on vacation this week).

Subject: OPM Hours Survey - January, 2001 - CHANGES!! PLEASE READ!


It's that time again to enter your hours and activities for January, 2001.  
Please use the shortcut below or go to the following path O:\Energy_Ops\OPM 
Hours Survey\ProdUser to access the hours survey.

PLEASE NOTE THAT THERE ARE SOME CHANGES THIS MONTH IN THE SURVEY.  THEY ARE 
AS FOLLOWS:

1) You must use your new SAP cost center in the survey this month.  I have 
attached a file that converts your old cost center incase you don't know what 
your new one is.

2) Due to the SAP cost center conversion, we were unable to roll over 
previous months commercial teams and headcount (FTE) information.  Therefore, 
we need you to enter the commercial teams your cost center supports and the 
FTE's in your cost center.  We will roll this information over beginning next 
month.

3) In previous months you were able to print a report that showed your prior 
months hours by activity.  Due to the SAP cost center conversion, that 
function is not available this month.  It will be available next month.  If 
you need your hours for prior months please call me and I will forward this 
information to you.

When completing the FTE's section of the survey, if there are any Director, 
Sr. Admin or Admin positions in your cost center, please complete 
accordingly.  You are not expected to complete a hours survey for these 
positions but we do need them to be included in your FTE's.

Please have your survey's completed by Wednesday, February 7.  Please call me 
if you have any questions or need me to help you complete the survey.

Thanks,
Suzanne
(X 5-7341)

input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace the monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) "Hours Survey" and "Activity Driver Survey" filled in by hand by ~50 managers with pre-filled data from existing systems (time/headcount from ATEs/SAP, driver counts from standard system reports), with managers only confirming or correcting exceptions.

TODAY: Every month the OPM team (Shari Mao, James Scribner, later Suzanne Nicholie) sends an hours survey to ~50 managers and an activity driver survey to ~23 managers. Each manager fills in hours by activity, commercial teams supported, FTEs, and driver quantities by RC, then returns it; the OPM team chases late responders, and the director escalates.
Evidence:
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2080.eml (Suzanne Nicholie, Feb 2001, sent to ~50 people): "It's that time again to enter your hours and activities for January, 2001." and "Due to the SAP cost center conversion, we were unable to roll over previous months commercial teams and headcount (FTE) information.  Therefore, we need you to enter the commercial teams your cost center supports and the FTE's in your cost center." Then reminder: "This is just a friendly reminder that the OPM Hours survey is due today."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1154.eml (James Scribner, May Activity Survey, 23 recipients): "Please select your RCs, and fill in the driver quantity for the requested driver for the month of May." and "If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the surveyed data, please send the report to Jennifer Reside.  This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1188.eml (Brenda Herod, 7 Jun 2000): "The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your concerns on the process burdening you."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1243.eml (June Hourly Survey to ~49 recipients): "If your hours have not changed from last month, please send us an email to indicate so."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/923.eml (Shari Mao to Daren Farmer): "ATEs shows that your team has one specialist for 1497 in January and February... we have not received a survey from this person.  This lack of information prevents your expenses from being 100% allocated out to the commercial teams." — the headcount data already exists in ATEs.
- Same surveys recur monthly: 1084.eml "April Activity Surveys", 998.eml "March Activity Survey", 1244.eml "Activity Survey - June 2000", 1319.eml "July Activity Driver Survey", 2015.eml "OPM Hours Survey - December, 2000".

CHANGE: OPM team pre-populates each manager's survey from last month's hours, ATEs/SAP headcount and cost centers, and pulls driver quantities directly from standard system reports (deal counts, path counts, etc.) as the survey sender herself proposed. Managers receive a pre-filled survey and only edit what changed; no "no change" emails; non-response defaults to last month's data, removing chase emails.

AFTER: Manager reviews a pre-filled form (~3-5 min) instead of building it; OPM team no longer chases.

SAVINGS (conservative): Hours survey: ~50 managers × 10 min saved = 500 min. Activity driver survey: ~23 managers × 10 min saved = 230 min. Chasing reminders/escalations (OPM staff + director) ~30 min. Total ≈ 760 min ≈ 12.7 h/month × $85 ≈ $1,077/month. Frequency: monthly per "fill out this survey every month" (1154.eml) and "It's that time again" (2080.eml). Note: the OPM team building the pre-fill feeds is a one-time setup; ongoing extract work by the OPM team is small, and I have netted it out by using only 10 of the ~15-20 minutes each manager spends.

Note: from Sept 2000 the hours survey moved to an Access tool (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml), but 2080.eml shows managers still enter hours, commercial teams and FTEs by hand monthly into it.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The idea might be sound, but the mail doesn't support most of the 10 minutes a day it claims to save.

**What checks out:**
- Ricky Archer at Calpine emailed `CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc` to an HPL scheduler, with other Enron staff copied. This ran from Dec 1999 to Nov 2000. The scheduler changed over time (Lloyd, then Lannou), and the copy list grew from Farmer to Farmer, Young, then Farmer, McCoy and Cotten. 22 files carry the subject.
- Revised nominations were resent as whole files (773.eml), there were weekend files (1330.eml), and there was a monthly nomination too (1245.eml).

**What doesn't hold up:**
1. **The "confirmed even when nothing changed" email is unreliable.** `corpus/giron-d/sent/795.eml` is the only support for this step, and it doesn't look like the rest of the archive:
   - It has no Date line.
   - Its message ID and sender line use different formats from Giron's other sent mail (`sent/99.eml` is a normal example).
   - Giron and Mary Poorman don't appear anywhere else in the Calpine nomination mail.
   
   It can't be used as evidence, and nothing else shows a confirmation reply.
2. **Re-keying is assumed, not shown.** No message says the scheduler types the .doc into a scheduling system, or how long that takes.
3. **The daily phone call is one sentence.** "As we spoke of this morning" (williams-w3/inbox/143.eml) shows one call on one day, not a duplicate call every day. The 2 minutes a day for it is unsupported.
4. **Little is left once those are removed.** What the mail shows is the scheduler opening one attachment and up to three copied people glancing at it. That is a few minutes a day at most, and the scheduler would still have to check volumes under the new system.
5. **Calpine would have to change how it works.** The plan depends on an outside company adopting a new feed or form. The proposal shows no sign that Calpine would agree, and it counts no cost for building and running the system.
6. **Frequency is plausible but not shown.** "Daily" in the subject makes about 21 a month believable, but the archive holds only 22 nominations in a year. A revised proposal should say that the archive kept only a sample.

**To fix it (more research could change the verdict):** find mail from the schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer, Young) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc. That could be entering it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors or late revisions. Also look for anything showing Calpine would accept a structured format. If that turns up, rebuild the estimate from those steps only. Drop the copied readers' time unless the mail shows they act on the nomination.

Files:
- `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\calpine-daily-nomination-reject.json`
- `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\corpus\giron-d\sent\795.eml` (the suspect message)

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The main problem is the idea itself: the organization had already built most of what it proposes. The evidence also misreads the key message.

**What's wrong:**

1. **Carrying forward last month's data already existed.** From September 2000 the hours survey moved to an Access tool (1415.eml, 1436.eml). By December 2000 it showed each cost center's hours from the prior month (2015.eml: "There is a new report that shows your cost center's hours from the prior month"). In 2080.eml, re-entering commercial teams and FTEs was a one-off caused by the SAP cost center changeover: "Due to the SAP cost center conversion, we were unable to roll over previous months commercial teams and headcount (FTE) information… We will roll this information over beginning next month." The same message says the prior-month hours report "will be available next month." So the proposal's note that "2080.eml shows managers still enter hours, commercial teams and FTEs by hand monthly" is wrong. That message describes the exception, not the routine.
2. **Pulling driver counts from reports was already offered.** The proposal credits this idea to the survey sender, but 1154.eml shows it was already the policy: "If your group currently generates a standard report… send the report to Jennifer Reside. This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month." The mail also has no driver survey after August 2000 (1319.eml is the last), so the 23 × 10 minutes a month for that survey isn't supported after then.
3. **Hours by activity can't come from ATEs/SAP.** ATEs gives headcount (923.eml), not how each team's time splits across activities and commercial teams. That split is the manager's own judgment and is what the survey collects (84.eml). A system can't pre-fill it beyond last month's figures, which the tool already showed.
4. **The savings are inflated.** The 500 minutes for the hours survey assumes managers rebuild everything every month. The chasing figure comes from the May 2000 spreadsheet era (1188.eml), before the Access tool.

**Research that could rescue it:** find what managers still did by hand each month in the Access tool after January 2001, such as the team percentage splits in 84.eml, and how long it took. Also check whether driver surveys continued after August 2000. A proposal sized on that remaining work alone might hold up, but it would be much smaller.

The rejection file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\opm-survey-prefill-reject.json`.

Proposal: Automatically detect and extend (or roll) Sitara deals when gas flows at a meter outside the deal term, instead of Volume Management emailing the trader meter-by-meter.

TODAY: Allocation exception / bridgeback reports show meters with flow but no valid deal (deal expired, evergreen flag missing or not working, flow a day before start or after end). Volume Management (Fred Boas, Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Sherlyn Schumack) emails the desk lead Daren Farmer per meter asking him to extend or create a deal; meanwhile the gas sits on Strangers Gas; once extended, settlements builds an accounting arrangement and redrafts invoices. Same meters recur month after month.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/749.eml (Fred Boas -> Aimee Lannou -> Daren, Feb 2000): "There is a bridgeback error at the above referenced meter and month.  The reason for the error is that the deal, # 97929 has expired." and Aimee: "Is there a way for you to extend the deal or create a new one since there seems to be a little bit of flow each month?"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/750.eml (Aimee Lannou, meter 7266): "An accounting arrangement is always created every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/801.eml: "Meters 3002 and 3003 have volume from Jan 99 thru the current month.  Could a deal be created for these volumes? There is a substanital amount of volume each month." and Fred Boas: "Following is a list of allocation exceptions on Daily Swing meters that must be fixed."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1021.eml (Jackie Young, Apr 2000): "I hate to be a pest but here's the deal on the above two meters:" ... "Sitara deal #214948 expired 3/27/2000.  No evergreen and no new deal referenced.  This is a little premature but this meter is active   monthly"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/899.eml (Mar 2000): "98-9676  Sitara Deal #151669 Deal good from 1/1/00 - 1/31/00 but there is flow for all of February 2000 with no K." and "I'm going to place 98-9676 on Strangers Gas until you hear back from Daren or Julie."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1406.eml (Sep 2000): Daren: "Please review deal 133010.  The deal shows evergreen, but nothing rolled to September." Julie Meyers: "This deal was not put in right."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1981.eml (Dec 2000, Enerfin meter 980439): "Daren can you please extend Deal #422516 to cover flow  of 9 dec. for 10/6/2000 and extend deal 432556 to cover flow of 44 dec. for 10/19/2000?" ... "Volume Mgmt is trying to clear up these issues." The thread passes through Sherlyn Schumack, Jackie Young, Victor Lamadrid, Rita Wynne and Daren over a week for 53 MMBtu ("Deal 422516 (Purchase from Dynegy) needs to be extended for these 2 days so I can do an accounting arrangement.").
- A grep for phrases like "extend the deal", "create a deal", "set up a deal", "deal for meter" finds 55 files in farmer-d/logistics alone (Dec 1999–Mar 2001), e.g. 1018, 1041, 1129, 1158, 1221, 1274, 1386, 1403, 1457, 1543, 2023, 2077, 2095.

CHANGE: (1) A nightly job compares POPS/MOPS meter flow to Sitara deal terms and produces an exception list (meter, days, volume, last deal, counterparty) sent to the responsible trader with the proposed extension prefilled; (2) a rule auto-extends the last valid deal at the same price terms for overflow within a tolerance (e.g. ≤ 2 days or small volume) on meters that flow monthly, flagged for trader review; (3) the evergreen flag is validated against the contract term at deal entry so it rolls correctly. Strangers-gas parking and the accounting arrangement step disappear for these cases.

AFTER: Trader approves a prefilled list once a day/week (~1 min per item); no back-and-forth emails between volume management, settlements and trader; no accounting arrangement needed.

SAVINGS per incident (all people): requester investigates and writes email ~10 min; trader looks up deal/contract and extends ~10 min; settlements builds accounting arrangement and redrafts ~10 min; follow-ups/chasers ~5 min. ≈35 min → ~5 min after (review/approve) = 30 min saved. Frequency: the archive is partial, but even it shows 55+ such files in 16 months (~3.5/month) and many threads cover 2–4 meters each; requesters say the same meters flow "each month" (749, 801) and need an arrangement "always created every month" (750). Conservatively 8 incidents/month × 30 min = 240 min = 4 h/month × $85 = $340/month.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

tool_use_result.prompt:
Proposal: Automatically detect and extend (or roll) Sitara deals when gas flows at a meter outside the deal term, instead of Volume Management emailing the trader meter-by-meter.

TODAY: Allocation exception / bridgeback reports show meters with flow but no valid deal (deal expired, evergreen flag missing or not working, flow a day before start or after end). Volume Management (Fred Boas, Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Sherlyn Schumack) emails the desk lead Daren Farmer per meter asking him to extend or create a deal; meanwhile the gas sits on Strangers Gas; once extended, settlements builds an accounting arrangement and redrafts invoices. Same meters recur month after month.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/749.eml (Fred Boas -> Aimee Lannou -> Daren, Feb 2000): "There is a bridgeback error at the above referenced meter and month.  The reason for the error is that the deal, # 97929 has expired." and Aimee: "Is there a way for you to extend the deal or create a new one since there seems to be a little bit of flow each month?"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/750.eml (Aimee Lannou, meter 7266): "An accounting arrangement is always created every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/801.eml: "Meters 3002 and 3003 have volume from Jan 99 thru the current month.  Could a deal be created for these volumes? There is a substanital amount of volume each month." and Fred Boas: "Following is a list of allocation exceptions on Daily Swing meters that must be fixed."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1021.eml (Jackie Young, Apr 2000): "I hate to be a pest but here's the deal on the above two meters:" ... "Sitara deal #214948 expired 3/27/2000.  No evergreen and no new deal referenced.  This is a little premature but this meter is active   monthly"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/899.eml (Mar 2000): "98-9676  Sitara Deal #151669 Deal good from 1/1/00 - 1/31/00 but there is flow for all of February 2000 with no K." and "I'm going to place 98-9676 on Strangers Gas until you hear back from Daren or Julie."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1406.eml (Sep 2000): Daren: "Please review deal 133010.  The deal shows evergreen, but nothing rolled to September." Julie Meyers: "This deal was not put in right."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1981.eml (Dec 2000, Enerfin meter 980439): "Daren can you please extend Deal #422516 to cover flow  of 9 dec. for 10/6/2000 and extend deal 432556 to cover flow of 44 dec. for 10/19/2000?" ... "Volume Mgmt is trying to clear up these issues." The thread passes through Sherlyn Schumack, Jackie Young, Victor Lamadrid, Rita Wynne and Daren over a week for 53 MMBtu ("Deal 422516 (Purchase from Dynegy) needs to be extended for these 2 days so I can do an accounting arrangement.").
- A grep for phrases like "extend the deal", "create a deal", "set up a deal", "deal for meter" finds 55 files in farmer-d/logistics alone (Dec 1999–Mar 2001), e.g. 1018, 1041, 1129, 1158, 1221, 1274, 1386, 1403, 1457, 1543, 2023, 2077, 2095.

CHANGE: (1) A nightly job compares POPS/MOPS meter flow to Sitara deal terms and produces an exception list (meter, days, volume, last deal, counterparty) sent to the responsible trader with the proposed extension prefilled; (2) a rule auto-extends the last valid deal at the same price terms for overflow within a tolerance (e.g. ≤ 2 days or small volume) on meters that flow monthly, flagged for trader review; (3) the evergreen flag is validated against the contract term at deal entry so it rolls correctly. Strangers-gas parking and the accounting arrangement step disappear for these cases.

AFTER: Trader approves a prefilled list once a day/week (~1 min per item); no back-and-forth emails between volume management, settlements and trader; no accounting arrangement needed.

SAVINGS per incident (all people): requester investigates and writes email ~10 min; trader looks up deal/contract and extends ~10 min; settlements builds accounting arrangement and redrafts ~10 min; follow-ups/chasers ~5 min. ≈35 min → ~5 min after (review/approve) = 30 min saved. Frequency: the archive is partial, but even it shows 55+ such files in 16 months (~3.5/month) and many threads cover 2–4 meters each; requesters say the same meters flow "each month" (749, 801) and need an arrangement "always created every month" (750). Conservatively 8 incidents/month × 30 min = 240 min = 4 h/month × $85 = $340/month.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

I updated the June transport usage tickets today through HPL, and will be 
finishing these tickets tomorrow.  Rates have been updated to reflect current 
matrix rates and all baseload rates that I know of at this time.  I have not 
yet received third party transport rates, so if you know of any, please let 
me know.  Also, I have zeroed out some volumes on some tickets for June, so 
your schedulers will have to update volumes as they know them.  Rule of thumb 
was that if I had to add a month, I refreshed the rate but left volume at 
zero.  If the months were already on the ticket, then I refreshed the rate 
and left the volume as is.

I would advise that your schedulers check volumes on all pipes to ensure 
they're reflected in Position Manager correctly.  Please let me know if you 
have any questions.  All pipes will be updated by tomorrow morning.

Heidi

input.description: Transport usage ticket rate refresh proposal
input.prompt:
Proposal: Automatically roll the monthly Sitara transport usage tickets forward and populate their rates from the transport rate matrix / Unify rate tables, instead of a person refreshing every pipe's ticket by hand each month.

TODAY: Each month before the flow month, Heidi Withers (Energy Ops, transport rates) goes through every pipe's transport usage tickets in Sitara, adds the new month, re-keys rates from Lauri Allen's rate matrix plus any known baseload/third-party rates, and zeroes volumes on months she adds; schedulers then must re-enter/check volumes on all pipes in Position Manager, and she runs a Basis Adjustment report afterwards to double-check rates. The correct rates already exist in Unify (used for invoicing), so the tickets duplicate data that lives elsewhere; when the tickets are wrong the desk P&L during the month is off.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml (24 May 2000, "June Transport Usage Tickets"): "I updated the June transport usage tickets today through HPL, and will be finishing these tickets tomorrow.  Rates have been updated to reflect current matrix rates and all baseload rates that I know of at this time." and "I have zeroed out some volumes on some tickets for June, so your schedulers will have to update volumes as they know them." and "I would advise that your schedulers check volumes on all pipes to ensure they're reflected in Position Manager correctly."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml (25 May 2000): "The tickets are finished." ... "Dave, once volumes get attached to these tickets, I would like to run a Basis Adjustment report by pipe to double-check the desk rates."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml (30 Jun 2000, "July Transport Usage Tickets"): "I have input and updated transport usage tickets for July." and "I do not yet know what baseload rates you have agreed upon, so you will need to adjust them in the appropriate tickets."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/867.eml (2 Mar 2000): "The rates are in the system correctly in Unify (so that we can invoice correctly), but Daren's group uses a Sitara deal (the transport usage tickets) to estimate desk transport in the P&L during the month." ... "By not having the right rates on the transport usage tickets, the risk is that the P&L will be off during the month." and "Lauri's matrix shows 0.05 from Thompsonville to HSC, but the transport usage ticket (updated by Daren's group) has 0.055."; also "the economics group publishes this report every month to show how much the marketing desk spent in transport."

CHANGE: Make the usage tickets term/evergreen per pipe path and have Sitara look up the matrix rate (the same rate table Unify invoices from) by path and month, instead of storing a keyed rate. Volumes carry forward from the prior month (no zeroing). Only exceptions — newly agreed baseload or third-party rates — are entered by hand, by whoever agrees them.

AFTER: No monthly ticket rebuild; ~1 hour/month for Heidi to enter exception rates and run the Basis Adjustment check; schedulers no longer re-key volumes zeroed by the refresh.

SAVINGS: Heidi's monthly refresh spans two working days ("today… will be finishing these tickets tomorrow", "All pipes will be updated by tomorrow morning"); conservatively 6 hours of her time → 1 hour = 5 h saved. Scheduler volume re-entry on zeroed tickets: conservatively 3 desks/schedulers (to: Baumbach, Clynes, Farmer) × 20 min = 1 h saved. Total ≈ 6 h/month × $85 = $510/month. Frequency: monthly — the tickets are refreshed per flow month (June in 1144/1145, July in 1257, February review in 867). Not counted: the P&L accuracy benefit from rates tying to the matrix.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

toolu_016nrGCD4XGBvUQM5SYn3hmT.prompt:
Proposal: Automatically roll the monthly Sitara transport usage tickets forward and populate their rates from the transport rate matrix / Unify rate tables, instead of a person refreshing every pipe's ticket by hand each month.

TODAY: Each month before the flow month, Heidi Withers (Energy Ops, transport rates) goes through every pipe's transport usage tickets in Sitara, adds the new month, re-keys rates from Lauri Allen's rate matrix plus any known baseload/third-party rates, and zeroes volumes on months she adds; schedulers then must re-enter/check volumes on all pipes in Position Manager, and she runs a Basis Adjustment report afterwards to double-check rates. The correct rates already exist in Unify (used for invoicing), so the tickets duplicate data that lives elsewhere; when the tickets are wrong the desk P&L during the month is off.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml (24 May 2000, "June Transport Usage Tickets"): "I updated the June transport usage tickets today through HPL, and will be finishing these tickets tomorrow.  Rates have been updated to reflect current matrix rates and all baseload rates that I know of at this time." and "I have zeroed out some volumes on some tickets for June, so your schedulers will have to update volumes as they know them." and "I would advise that your schedulers check volumes on all pipes to ensure they're reflected in Position Manager correctly."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml (25 May 2000): "The tickets are finished." ... "Dave, once volumes get attached to these tickets, I would like to run a Basis Adjustment report by pipe to double-check the desk rates."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml (30 Jun 2000, "July Transport Usage Tickets"): "I have input and updated transport usage tickets for July." and "I do not yet know what baseload rates you have agreed upon, so you will need to adjust them in the appropriate tickets."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/867.eml (2 Mar 2000): "The rates are in the system correctly in Unify (so that we can invoice correctly), but Daren's group uses a Sitara deal (the transport usage tickets) to estimate desk transport in the P&L during the month." ... "By not having the right rates on the transport usage tickets, the risk is that the P&L will be off during the month." and "Lauri's matrix shows 0.05 from Thompsonville to HSC, but the transport usage ticket (updated by Daren's group) has 0.055."; also "the economics group publishes this report every month to show how much the marketing desk spent in transport."

CHANGE: Make the usage tickets term/evergreen per pipe path and have Sitara look up the matrix rate (the same rate table Unify invoices from) by path and month, instead of storing a keyed rate. Volumes carry forward from the prior month (no zeroing). Only exceptions — newly agreed baseload or third-party rates — are entered by hand, by whoever agrees them.

AFTER: No monthly ticket rebuild; ~1 hour/month for Heidi to enter exception rates and run the Basis Adjustment check; schedulers no longer re-key volumes zeroed by the refresh.

SAVINGS: Heidi's monthly refresh spans two working days ("today… will be finishing these tickets tomorrow", "All pipes will be updated by tomorrow morning"); conservatively 6 hours of her time → 1 hour = 5 h saved. Scheduler volume re-entry on zeroed tickets: conservatively 3 desks/schedulers (to: Baumbach, Clynes, Farmer) × 20 min = 1 h saved. Total ≈ 6 h/month × $85 = $510/month. Frequency: monthly — the tickets are refreshed per flow month (June in 1144/1145, July in 1257, February review in 867). Not counted: the P&L accuracy benefit from rates tying to the matrix.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

Proposal: Add a booking rule in TAGG/EnronOnline so that any deal where the counterparty has a master swap with Enron Canada Corp (ECC) is routed straight into the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book (with ECC as the settling entity), plus a nightly exception report — replacing the monthly hunt-and-flip across every Houston book before Nymex close/invoicing.

TODAY: Each month at Nymex close, Stacey Vallejo (Calgary) searches Houston books for ECC/third-party deals, then emails ~5–8 Houston risk controllers (Gossett, Giron, Keiser, Kelly, Baumbach, McLaughlin, Guggenheim, Dawson, Johnson…) asking them to "go through all your books" and flip them; controllers (e.g. Darron Giron) forward to their 5–7 book administrators, who search and flip deals by hand and reply. EnronOnline deals land in the wrong book automatically. Invoicing for both ECC and ENA is held until it's fixed. Others ask to copy Darron's ad-hoc calc for finding them.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/giron-d/sent/539.eml (1 Nov 2000, to 8 controllers, forwarded by Darron to 5 book admins): "Just a quick request for you to go into all your books to make sure that there are no ECC deals booked there." ... "Invoicing for November should start today, and both ECC and ENA are held back from invoicing until these deals are fixed, as the deals will be invoiced by the wrong Enron counterparty if they aren't."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/550.eml (27 Oct 2000): "These are all EnronOnline deals so they were put into this book automatically." ... "Nymex closes today, and I'm going to have to start invoicing on Monday, so I need to have all deals with ECC in the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by the end of today."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/407.eml (8 Dec 2000): lists 12 deal IDs "in the MGMT-WEST book that need to be flipped to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book in the morning" and "Could you please make sure that there aren't any more deals with ECC and a third counterparty in this book as it messes up invoicing and settlement."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/360.eml (27 Dec 2000): "Just a friendly reminder for you to please go through all your books to make sure there aren't any deals between ECC and a third counterparty." and William Kelly: "Goss said you may have a calc set up to identify these deals.  Any chance I could copy it?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/195.eml (26 Feb 2001, forwarded by Darron to 7 book admins): "This is just a quick reminder for all of you to please go into all of your books and flip out all the deals that are supposed to settle with ECC and a third counterparty  to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by the end of the day today.  Nymex closes today"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/192.eml (26 Feb 2001): "ECC has now signed a Master Swap Agreement with Aquila Canada Corp., and all deals traded with ENA and Aquila Canada Corp. need to be settled with ECC in the P& book.  These deals are showing up in TAGG as settling with ENA, could you all please keep an eye out for deals with this company and flip them right away."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/114.eml (28 Mar 2001): Stacey lists books searched (FT-CENT, FT-NORTHWEST, FT-ONTARIO, FT-WEST, GD-CENTRAL, NG-EXOTIC, NG-PRICE) and "If you find any others that I might have missed, please flip them."
- Same cycle in 21 files: Oct 2000 (550, 551), Nov (539, 535, 460, 459), Dec (419, 407, 406, 360), Jan 2001 (292), Feb (270, 250, 246, 195, 192), Mar (168, 164, 114, 108), May (23).

CHANGE: Maintain the list of ECC master-swap counterparties in Global Counterparty (it already exists for settlement); add a TAGG/EOL routing rule so deals with those counterparties under ECC terms book directly to FT-US/CAND-ERMS; a nightly report lists any ECC/third-party deals still in other books for the owning book admin. Remove the monthly all-books sweep and reminder chain.

AFTER: Stacey adds new master-swap counterparties to the list when signed (minutes, occasional); book admins fix the rare exception from the nightly report.

SAVINGS per monthly cycle (Enron people only): Stacey searching books and writing lists/reminders ~45 min; ~6 controllers each checking their books/forwarding ~15 min = 90 min; ~6 book admins (Darron's forward lists 5–7) searching and flipping ~10 min each = 60 min. ≈195 min → ~15 min residual = 180 min = 3 h/month × $85 = $255/month. Frequency: at least monthly, tied to Nymex close / invoicing ("Invoicing for November should start today", "Nymex closes today"), and the archive shows the cycle in 7 of the 8 months Oct 2000–May 2001, often several messages a month. Not counted: invoicing delays for ECC and ENA.

I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The problem is mainly the idea as designed. The mail also gives weak support for the time it claims to save.

**What holds up:**
- Heidi Withers does refresh the transport usage tickets in Sitara before each flow month. She did June over 24–25 May 2000 (1144, 1145) and July on 30 June 2000 (1257).
- Rates are keyed in by hand from Lauri Allen's rate matrix.
- Ticket rates that don't match the matrix make the desk P&L wrong during the month (867).

**What is wrong:**
1. **"Evergreen" tickets don't fit what the mail says Sitara can do.** In 1796.eml, Sabrae Zajac writes that usage tickets "can only be set up for approx. 3 months at a time". She had to set up 7 tickets to cover 19 months. The proposal never mentions this limit.
2. **Unify's rates may not exist yet when the tickets need them.** In 867.eml, Heidi says the Unify rates are there "so that we can invoice correctly". Her group has focused on "settling the G/L (after the month is over)". The tickets are built before the flow month, when baseload and third-party rates are often still unknown: "I have not yet received third party transport rates" (1144) and "I do not yet know what baseload rates you have agreed upon" (1257). A rate lookup can't fill in rates nobody has agreed yet, and those are the rates that cost the hand work.
3. **Carrying volumes forward doesn't save the schedulers anything.** They still have to enter each month's actual volumes. Copying last month's numbers just leaves wrong figures to correct, so the 1 hour a month saved for schedulers isn't real.
4. **The 6 hours of Heidi's time is a guess.** The mail only shows the work running from one day into the next morning. Only two refreshes are on record, and before March 2000 Daren's group kept the tickets (867). So the claim that it happens every month rests on two months.

**Research that could support a revised proposal:**
- Mail stating how long a refresh actually takes.
- Whether Sitara can hold longer-term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month.
- Refreshes in months other than June and July 2000.

With that evidence, a smaller change, such as an automatic check of ticket rates against the matrix, could be costed and proposed.

Rejection file: C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\transport-usage-ticket-rollforward-reject.json

Jeff, 
Thanks for the lead with Avril Forster, it looks like that will help us in 
the near future.  Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, 
we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market 
valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio.

Desk heads,

Can you provide to Ellen and myself the names of the person on your desk who 
we should go to with these requests.  Also, please let these persons know 
that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several 
per week).

Here's the background of these requests.  Because of various accounting 
rules, Parties dealing in Derivatives must show third party valuations to 
their Auditors.  Our group (Confirmations) is responsible for providing MTM 
values and open position reports for these parties.  We do not have access to 
any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line 
"EnTelligence" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us 
to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without 
having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book.

Thanks for the help.  We'll try to get these off of your plates as soon as 
possible.

Joe

  "today": "Allocation-exception and bridgeback reports show meters where gas flowed but no valid Sitara deal covers the day: the deal expired, the evergreen flag was missing or did not roll, or flow came a day before the start or after the end. A Volume Management analyst (Fred Boas, Aimee Lannou, Jackie Young) looks up the last deal and emails the desk lead, Daren Farmer, one meter at a time, asking him to extend the deal or create a new one. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
19	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. Proposal: Give the Confirmations group a self-service counterparty MTM / open-position report as of past dates (the "EnTelligence with back-dated curves" they already want), so counterparty audit-confirmation requests no longer go to every Risk desk head and down to a book analyst.

TODAY: Counterparties' auditors ask Enron for third-party MTM valuations. Confirmations (Joe Hunter, Ellen Wallumrod) has no valuation system, so for each counterparty request they email all 5–6 gas desk heads (Gossett, Keiser, Love, Giron, McLaughlin, Baumbach); each desk head forwards to an analyst, who runs/export the mini-book for that counterparty as of the past date, blacks out Delta/Vol columns, totals it, and replies; the desk head forwards the answer back.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/giron-d/sent/241.eml (Joe Hunter, 8 Feb 2001, "Audit Request procedure", to 6 desk heads): "Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio." ... "please let these persons know that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several per week)." ... "We do not have access to any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line "EnTelligence" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book." Darron: "Call Pat Ryder for West desk requests."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/240.eml (9 Feb 2001, to 5 desk heads, forwarded by Darron to Patrick Ryder): "Please forward to Ellen Wallumrod the MTM valuation(mini-book) for all CoEnergy Trading Company deals as of Dec 31, 2000.  If you can export into excel and forward by e-mail, that would be appreciated."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/214.eml (16 Feb 2001, to 6 desk heads, forwarded to Ryder): "Can you provide MTM values as of Dec 29, 2000, for the short name of CROSS TIMBERS."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/137.eml (21 Mar 2001, Gossett to 5 desk heads, forwarded by Darron to Carole Frank): "Two more counterparties need MTM values for Dec. 29, 2000." ... "Please provide the total MTM value for that date within your region."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/136.eml: Carole Frank's reply to Darron, forwarded by Darron to Gossett: "The following are the totals for Tudor BVI and Ospraie.  The total MTM value for the West Desk are as follows.  Detail can be found in the attachment." — shows the 4-hop chain (Confirmations → desk head → analyst → desk head → back).

CHANGE: Build (or prioritise the already-planned) EnTelligence/report that values a counterparty's deals across all books as of a chosen official close date using stored official curves, with Greeks suppressed. Confirmations runs it themselves.

AFTER: Confirmations runs one report per request (they already handle and send each request, so their time is roughly unchanged); no desk heads or Risk analysts involved.

SAVINGS per request (Risk side only, since Confirmations' handling is not removed): ~5 desk heads read/forward/return ~3 min each = 15 min; analysts on the ~3 desks that have deals with the counterparty pull the mini-book as of the past date, export to Excel, black out Delta/Vol, total and reply ~15 min each = 45 min. ≈60 min saved per request. content.text:
I saved the proposal, but its value is much smaller than you estimated: **$57.80 a month**, not $340. That is 25 minutes × 1.64 times a month = 0.68 hours. It is item 5 of 5 in decisions.md.

**What holds up.** The work is real and keeps coming back. All your quotes match the mail. Daren Farmer's mailbox has about 24 separate requests from Feb 2000 to Mar 2001 asking him to extend or create a deal. Some meters come back in later months: 1517 in Mar 2000 and Jan 2001, and 98-6725 in 1018 and 1021. No saved or rejected entry covers this work. The closest are the monthly transport usage ticket roll and the Strangers Gas write-off memos, which are different work.

**What I changed:**
- **How often.** The pipeline counts separate incidents in the mail; it does not use your 8 a month. Your 55 grep matches include many replies in the same threads: 1977, 1981, 1983, 1987, 1999 and 2003 are only two incidents, the Enerfin meter 980439 thread and the 98-439 deal extension thread. Some matches are other topics, such as Shoreline, Black Marlin and El Paso. Separate threads come to about 1.6 a month, so 8 a month is not supported. I left the stated rate empty, because nothing in the mail gives a count across the organization.
- **Minutes.** I used 25 rather than 30 a time. Many incidents are one request and one reply. The 30 assumed an invoice redraft step, which the mail does not show.
- **Wrong facts.**
  - Sherlyn Schumack works in settlements (she creates the accounting arrangements), not Volume Management.
  - Nothing in the mail shows invoices being redrafted.
  - The 1981 thread runs four days, 12/15 to 12/19, not a week.
- **Safeguards.** I kept trader approval rather than extending deals automatically at the same price. Daren asked that wellhead deals go through Tom Acton first (899). Another message (2095) shows that a deal with an inactive or suspended counterparty cannot be extended. In 1406, the evergreen flag was wrong because the contract itself had no evergreen. So the design flags these cases instead of extending them.

**How to raise the figure.** Look for the same requests in other traders' or schedulers' mailboxes. Volume Management (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou) sends them across desks, so the real organization-wide rate is probably higher than what one trader's folder shows.

The saved proposal is at C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\deal-extension-exceptions.json

Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill managers' monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys from ATEs/SAP and system reports so managers only correct exceptions.. Why: The organization had already built most of this: from late 2000 the Access hours survey carries forward commercial teams and FTEs and shows prior-month hours, and the driver survey already let groups send a standard report instead. The proposal mistakes a one-off January 2001 SAP glitch for the normal monthly process, and hours by activity cannot be taken from ATEs/SAP. Research that could settle it: Find what managers still do by hand each month in the Access tool after the January 2001 SAP changeover (for example, splitting hours by activity and team, as in 84.eml), how long it takes, and whether any driver surveys were still sent after August 2000; then size only that remaining work.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pull activity driver counts from Sitara/Unify reports and make the hours survey exception-only, carrying last month's hours forward. Why: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.
- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull driver counts from system reports and pre-fill hours from the prior month so managers only confirm.. Why: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale at zero price for the whole term and set the HPL/ENA demand tickets as index formulas, so each month needs only one crude value entry.. Why: The swap covered only January to May 2001 and its bookings were done as a one-time cleanup months later, not as monthly work, so there is no ongoing work for the change to save.
- Self-service counterparty MTM valuations for audit requests: Finish EnTelligence (or an equivalent read-only report) with back-dated curves so Confirmations values counterparty portfolios without routing requests through the Risk desks.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
- Backdated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only counterparty MTM report with back-dated curves so they answer auditor requests themselves instead of emailing every desk.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241) and proposes the same report.
- HPL Strangers Gas write-off approvals: Replace one printed, signed memo per meter with a monthly exception list, electronic approval and automatic write-off of small volumes. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. The mail shows neither: about a quarter to a third of lines are repeats, and the Louis Dreyfus target entity changes from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk or Carole Frank (for example Carole's replies, or desk-specific rebook requests like giron-d/sent/124.eml), count only those, and count how many are recurring entity pairs with one fixed target.
- Monthly transport usage ticket refresh in Sitara: Make Sitara transport usage tickets evergreen per pipe path, look up rates from the matrix/Unify rate tables, and carry volumes forward instead of a monthly hand refresh.. Why: The proposed design conflicts with the mail: Sitara usage tickets can only be set up for about 3 months at a time (1796.eml), Unify rates are entered for settlement after the month rather than before it (867.eml), and carrying last month's volumes forward would put wrong volumes in place, so the scheduler savings are not real and the 5 hours saved for Heidi is a guess based on a two-day span. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many hours the monthly refresh actually takes, whether Sitara can hold term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month, and refreshes in months other than June and July 2000, so that a smaller change (such as a rate check against the matrix) can be costed.
- Audit MTM valuation requests by counterparty: Give Confirmations a back-dated MTM report by counterparty that they run themselves, so audit requests stop going to every risk desk.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240, 241, plus 136).
- Weekly manual compact of WeaponX databases: Compact each desk's WeaponX file automatically every night instead of having each book admin do it by hand every week.. Why: The same work and change is already saved in decisions.md as item 2, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml).
- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Block known wrong-entity counterparties at TAGG deal entry with a credit-kept 'use instead' mapping, and route each Credit Report row to the owning book administrator.. Why: The 65 minutes a day rests on a 'fixed mapping' that the mail contradicts (the Aquila/Utilicorp rebook runs in opposite directions, the Louis Dreyfus target changes, and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is rebooked to itself), on a repeat rate of half when the cited reports show about a third, and on six desk heads forwarding every day when only Giron's forwards, often sent days late in batches, appear in the mail. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs that always have the same target. Find mail from book administrators or Confirmations, such as Julie Brewer's chase in 124.eml, that shows who actually rebooks and how long it takes. Check whether desk heads other than Giron forward the report at all, given that the book administrators are already on its distribution list.
- Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX databases: Have WeaponX compact itself automatically (scheduled overnight compact or Compact on Close) so book admins stop doing it by hand.. Why: The same work, citing the same two messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases'.
- Monthly search and flip of ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Auto-book ECC master-swap counterparty deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS at entry (EOL rule plus TAGG default) and send a nightly exception list to book owners.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/108, 114, 270, 292, 360).
- Rebooking deals to the right legal entity from the daily Credit Report: Add a credit-maintained alias table in TAGG that books known wrong entities to the approved one, and route each day's remaining exceptions by book instead of a desk lead forwarding the whole report. Why: The mail contradicts the fixed wrong-to-right pairs the alias table depends on (the same entity is sent to different targets, and Aquila/Utilicorp are rebooked in both directions), and the 9 minutes a day of West-desk rebooks, which make up half the savings, are not supported by anything in the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk's books and how long a rebook takes, and check across all the reports whether each wrong entity always goes to the same target (only about 10 of the ~70 forwarded reports have the list in the message body).

Why: The mail only shows Calpine emailing a .doc to the scheduler with Enron staff copied. 14	- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because it duplicates one that's already saved. The idea is sound, but `decisions.md` item 1, "Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests" ($1,694.05 a month), already covers the same work and the same change. It cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240 and 241). Three other duplicates of it had already been rejected. No more research would change this verdict.

**The evidence itself holds up.** I read all five messages and every quote is accurate. They show the chain: Confirmations emails every desk head, each forwards it to an analyst, and the answer comes back the same way. Joe Hunter writes "we recieve several per week", and the planned EnTelligence with back-dated curves is meant to take this "without taking up a Risk person's time". One small slip: Hunter's message is dated 8 Feb 2001, but file 241 is Darron Giron's reply from 9 Feb.

**A caution for the saved item.** Every request in the mail asks for values as of year-end 2000 (Dec 29 or Dec 31), and all were sent in February and March 2001. A search of the whole archive finds no other such requests. So "several per week" may describe year-end audit season, not a steady rate all year. If so, a monthly figure built from that rate, like the $1,694 a month on the saved item, may overstate the yearly savings. Requests dated in other months would show whether the rate holds year-round.

Bill

($1,694.05 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/136.eml, giron-d/sent/137.eml, giron-d/sent/214.eml, giron-d/sent/240.eml, giron-d/sent/241.eml

5:3. Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing: Book Canadian-settled deals straight into FT-US/CAND-ERMS, and send each book owner a nightly list of any that land elsewhere, instead of a monthly manual search of every Houston book. ($298.35 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/108.eml, giron-d/sent/114.eml, giron-d/sent/195.eml, giron-d/sent/270.eml, giron-d/sent/292.eml, giron-d/sent/360.eml, giron-d/sent/539.eml, giron-d/sent/550.eml

Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen's gas testing: Save every book's month-end and daily P&L top pages and curve shift reports to a read-only audit folder at month-end, so the auditors stop sending requests to the desks. ($255.00 a month). Cites giron-d/inbox/190.eml, giron-d/sent/201.eml, giron-d/sent/299.eml, giron-d/sent/317.eml, giron-d/sent/420.eml, giron-d/sent/515.eml, giron-d/sent/516.eml, giron-d/sent/583.eml

Monthly roll of Sitara transport usage tickets: A month-end job extends each active usage ticket, fills its rate from the matrix/Unify rates and carries last month's volume, leaving people only an exception list. ($198.05 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml, farmer-d/logistics/867.eml

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because it's a duplicate. The idea is sound, but `decisions.md` already has it saved as item 3, "Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing" ($298.35 a month). That entry proposes the same change (book these deals straight into FT-US/CAND-ERMS, plus a nightly list of stragglers for each book owner). It also cites the same messages: giron-d/sent/108, 114, 195, 270, 292, 360, 539 and 550. `check` flagged that 6 of this proposal's 9 occurrences are already occurrences of that saved entry. Another critic had already rejected a third version of the same idea on the same grounds. More research would not change the verdict.

Before checking for duplicates I verified the evidence and corrected the draft:

- **The quotes hold.** Every quoted line appears word for word in the cited files. The cycle runs from Oct 2000 to May 2001, and `check` counted it at once a month. At 180 minutes a cycle that comes to $255 a month, which is realistic.
- **One claim had no support.** The mail doesn't show that Global Counterparty keeps a list of ECC master-swap counterparties. It only says books must be added to Global Counterparty before they go into TAGG (giron-d/sent/755, 769). I removed that claim.
- **One important fact was missing.** In giron-d/sent/292.eml, Stacey says EnronOnline already books TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada deals to settle with ECC automatically. She has also asked Jennifer Denny at EnronOnline to set up the same for Duke. So the change extends a rule that already exists rather than building a new one. That makes it more feasible, but managers checking the mail would see the original wording as overstated. If item 3 doesn't mention this, it would be worth adding there.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\`:
- `ecc-deal-book-routing.json` (corrected draft, not saved)
- `ecc-deal-book-routing-reject.json` (the rejection, recorded in `decisions.md`)

input.prompt:
Proposal: Generate Transwestern's weekly "California Capacity Report" automatically from pipeline flow data and the Gas Daily price feed, instead of a marketer compiling and typing it every Friday.

TODAY: Every Friday Michelle Lokay (TW marketing) compiles a hand-typed email to the TW commercial team (Harris, Watson, Lindberg, Lohman, Donoho, McConnell, Y'barbo; cc Audrey Robertson): week-average TW deliveries to California with % of capacity, San Juan lateral throughput, East deliveries; El Paso deliveries to California by delivery point (PG&ETop, SoCalEhr, SoCalTop) with capacity, deliveries and %; Friday's Gas Daily prices with day changes; and EnronOnline basis by season. All numbers are averages/percentages computed by hand from pipeline flow data and published prices. Hand-typing causes errors: on 11 Jan 2002 she sent last week's figures under the old title and then had to resend a correction.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/lokay-m/inbox/10.eml (26 Oct 2001), "California Capacity Report for Week of 10/22-10/26": "Transwestern's average deliveries to California were 945 MMBtu/d (87%), with San Juan lateral throughput at 865 MMBtu/d.  Total East deliveries averaged 525 MMBtu/d." ... "El Paso's average deliveries to California were 1782 MMBtu/d (66%):" ... "- PG&ETop, capacity of 1140 MMBtu/d, deliveries of 667 MMBtu/d (59%)" ... "Friday's posted Gas Daily prices:" ... "Enron Online bases:"
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/110.eml (22 Feb 2002, week 02/19-02/22), same structure: "El Paso's average deliveries to California were 2063 MMBtu/d (70%):"
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/47.eml (11 Jan 2002 06:30) "FW: California Capacity Report for Week of 12/31-01/04" and corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/46.eml (11 Jan 2002 09:02) "RE: California Capacity Report for Week of 01/07-01/11": "Sorry, the effective date for this new report is 01/07-01/11." — a correction resend to all 7 recipients.
- Weekly cadence: 18 files carry the subject across Oct 2001–Mar 2002, one per week, e.g. sent_items/18.eml (12/10-12/14), 67.eml (12/17-12/21), 63.eml (12/26-12/28), 55.eml (12/31-01/04), 40.eml (01/14-01/18), 30.eml (01/21-01/25), 79.eml (01/28-02/01), 86.eml (02/04-02/08), 97.eml (02/11-02/15), 117.eml (02/25-03/01), 131.eml (03/04-03/08), 146.eml (03/11-03/15), 159.eml (03/18-03/22). The subject itself names the week.

CHANGE: A scheduled query pulls the week's scheduled/actual deliveries for TW (California deliveries, San Juan lateral, East) and El Paso's California delivery points from the posted EBB/flow data, computes averages and % of capacity, adds Friday's Gas Daily prices and changes, and emails or posts the report to the same list each Friday. Lokay adds commentary only if she wants.

AFTER: ~5 min Friday review/commentary; no hand calculation; no copy/date errors.

SAVINGS: Compiling ~10 averages and percentages from two pipelines' data plus 4 prices with changes and basis, then typing and sending: conservatively 30 min per week → 5 min = 25 min saved; plus occasional correction resends (not counted). Frequency: weekly (each subject names a Mon–Fri week; 16 consecutive weeks Dec 2001–Mar 2002 are present). 25 min × 4.33 weeks = 108 min ≈ 1.8 h/month × $85 ≈ $153/month. One-time build cost not counted.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

input.description: Monthly hand re-pricing of deals proposal
input.prompt:
Proposal: Stop re-pricing the same West-desk purchase deals by hand every month after settlements sees the counterparty invoice. Price them in Sitara by formula (index/crude components) or load the month's price in one batch from the desk's price calc before settlement, so settlements no longer emails the desk lead each month and waits.

TODAY: For at least three purchase deals whose price changes every month (EnerVest Sitara #27239, deal #27253, Agave deal at Hobbs/NNG), Sitara keeps last month's price. Settlements (Tricia Truong, Genaro Mendoza) compares to the counterparty's invoice, emails the West desk lead Darron Giron asking for a price change; Darron (later forwards to book admin Kristen Clause) edits Sitara and replies; settlements redrafts in Unify. Requests often wait weeks and need reminders.
Evidence (exact quotes):
- corpus/giron-d/sent/508.eml (Oct–Nov 2000): Tricia Truong: "I've already received invoice for 9/00 production.  Could you please change its price to 4.417791 (S#27239)?" ... "I just wanted to follow up on this issue with EnerVest." ... Dawn Kenne: "Darron, this is that wonderful Enervest issue." ... Bryce Baxter (9 Nov): "Darron - have you had a chance to take a look at this yet?" ... Darron (13 Nov): "It's done.  I appologize for this taking so long."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/469.eml (21 Nov 2000): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.878216 for Oct. 00 production?" Darron: "Done.  I did the 1999 changes as well."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/378.eml (20 Dec 2000): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.15544 for Nov. 00 Production ?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/301.eml (23 Jan 2001): "As usual, could you please change rate on S# 27239 for 12/00 production to $5.811329?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/141.eml (20 Mar 2001): "Could you please help me change the rate for the above Sitara # for Jan. 01 production to $9.624065?" Darron: "Please send these to Kristen Clause in the future."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/313.eml (Jan 2001): "Could you please change rate on the above deal from $2.24246 to $2.156695 for days 2/21/00 - 2/29/00?" then "This is just a friendly reminder....." then "Done.  Sorry it took so long."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/83.eml (6 Apr 2001, Genaro Mendoza): "Deal # 27253 has a price of $2.7423 for 03/01 production (this is the price used for 02/01). The customer invoiced ENA a price of $2.3043. Can you please update the deal in Sitara to reflect the correct price for 03/01?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/12.eml (8 May 2001): "Can you please update the 04/01 price for deal # 27253 in Sitara? It currently has a rate of $2.3043 (last month's price). The customer invoiced a rate of $1.8351."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/635.eml (Sep 2000, Agave): "Do you put together a spreadsheet calculating the price for gas purchases from Agave on NNG at the Hobbs Plant?" ... "For 08/00 production, there is a $.56 difference from what is in Sitara and what the customer invoiced us." Darron: "The Sitara was not updated for Aug.  I just corrected Sitara.  So you can redraft in Unify." Then "The difference in the price is in the value for Crude Merc."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/745.eml (Jul 2000): "Here is Agave for June.  I also made a change to May.  I was calculating the differential off of the wrong location index."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/300.eml (Jan 2001): "Can you please update the pricing for the 12/00 purchase from Agave (I believe it still has the 11/00 pricing) ?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/346.eml (Jan 2001): "We have had price discrepancies and they would like to go over the different pricing compnents to determine were we differ."

CHANGE: (a) Where the price follows a formula (Agave: crude Merc/index plus differential), set the Sitara deal to formula pricing from the official curves so it prices itself each month; (b) for the deals priced off the counterparty's monthly statement (EnerVest #27239, #27253), add them to a month-end "price-to-invoice" list that the book admin loads in one batch before settlements drafts, rather than one email per deal after the invoice arrives.

AFTER: No monthly per-deal request/reminder/forward chain; settlements drafts at the right price first time; one batch update per month by the book admin for statement-priced deals.

SAVINGS per deal-month (all people): settlements spots the mismatch, writes request ~5 min; desk lead reads/forwards ~3 min; reminder/chaser emails (shown in 508, 313) ~3 min average; redraft in Unify after correction ~5 min; book admin edit ~5 min → after: batch load ~3 min per deal and no redraft. ≈18 min saved per deal-month. 3 deals monthly (EnerVest monthly per "As usual" and Sep/Oct/Nov/Dec/Jan production requests; 27253 for Mar and Apr 2001 "last month's price"; Agave Jun, Aug, Dec 2000 production). 3 × 18 = 54 min ≈ 0.9 h/month × $85 ≈ $77/month. Plus Agave pricing errors (wrong location index, stale crude value) avoided — not counted.

No prompt-injection text found in these messages.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because the same work is already saved. Item 6 in `decisions.md`, "Weekly Transwestern California Capacity Report", is worth $88.40 a month and cites the same 16 messages. The check confirmed that all 16 of this proposal's cited messages are already used by that saved item. The idea itself is sound, so no further research would change the outcome.

If anyone revises the saved item, these errors in this draft should not be carried into it:

- **The 11 Jan 2002 mistake is described wrongly.** The 06:30 message (`sent_items/47.eml`) did not resend last week's figures. Its numbers (TW 855, 79%) differ from the real 12/31–01/04 report (`55.eml`: 840, 77%). It carried the new week's figures under the old week's title, sent as "FW:" of the old report. That points to Lokay editing last week's email as a template. The 09:02 resend (`46.eml`) only fixes the dates: "Sorry, the effective date for this new report is 01/07-01/11."
- **The week count is off by one.** From 12/10 to 03/22 there are 15 consecutive weeks, not 16. The 18 files are right, but `47.eml` and `46.eml` are one week, and `inbox/32.eml` repeats `sent_items/159.eml`.
- **The frequency is too high.** The proposal assumed 4.33 reports a month, but the mail has a gap between 26 Oct and 10 Dec. The check counts about 2.5 a month, so the realistic figure is about $88 a month, not $153.
- **Smaller points:**
  - EnronOnline basis was only in the report until December 2001. It shows as "n/a" in January and is gone by February.
  - The mail never says where the flow numbers come from, so "from the posted flow data" is a guess, not something the mail shows.

- `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\tw-california-capacity-report-reject.json` (rejection, recorded in `decisions.md`)
